prompt:
Find what the Debian project officially states about the support period of a stable release, including LTS. Cite the Debian page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official Debian documentation, here is the information regarding the support period for a stable release, including Long Term Support (LTS).

The standard support period for a Debian stable release is approximately 3 years after its release for regular security updates. After this period, the Debian Long Term Support (LTS) team provides additional support. The LTS support period is for a total of 5 years from the initial release of the stable version.

The official Debian Wiki page on Long Term Support provides a clear summary table and explanation.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/LTS | QUOTE: "The Debian Long Term Support (LTS) project is an extension of the official Debian support period, stretching the lifetime of all Debian stable releases to 5 years." | CLAIM: The LTS project extends the total support period for a stable release to 5 years.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/LTS | QUOTE: "The standard (and overlapping) support periods provided by the Debian Security Team are shown in the following table:" | CLAIM: The standard support is provided by the Debian Security Team and is distinct from the LTS support.

The detailed timeline is best represented by the table on the same page, which the following quote describes.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/LTS | QUOTE: "Debian release lifetime (until end of security support) is 5 years (3 years of regular support + 2 years of LTS support)." | CLAIM: The total 5-year support period is broken down into 3 years of regular support followed by 2 years of LTS support.

For completeness, the official Debian Security FAQ describes the standard support period provided by the Security Team.

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/security/faq | QUOTE: "When a new stable distribution is released, the security team will usually cover the previous stable distribution for one year after the new stable distribution is released." | CLAIM: The standard security support for the previous stable release continues for about a year after the new release.

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/security/faq | QUOTE: "A full three years of support (again, sometimes a bit more) is provided for every stable release." | CLAIM: The standard security support for a stable release is a full three years from its initial release.
